_comment: Rules the floor once shipped and has since withdrawn.
framework-install merges the floor into an existing settings.json and never
overwrites what it finds, which is the right default: it must not silently
undo a decision a repository made on purpose. The cost is that a rule the
floor REMOVES can never leave an installed repository, because merging only
That turned the 0.3.0 release into a no-op where it mattered most. 0.3.0
withdrew five coarse ask rules so that `docker exec api <test command>`,
`git branch -a` and a read-only `gh api` GET would stop prompting. Every
repository that had already installed 0.2.0 kept all five, ask still beat
allow, and the noise the release existed to remove did not move at all.
So withdrawal has to be recorded, not just performed. ef-doctor reports any
of these still present, and framework-install proposes removing them.
A rule belongs here only when the floor has taken over its job by a better
means — a narrower rule, or a guard that can read the whole command. This
is not a list of rules that were merely inconvenient.
Removal is always PROPOSED and never silent. A repository is allowed to
have re-added one of these on purpose, and the human is the one who knows.

retired.reason: a prefix rule cannot tell `docker exec api <test command>` from `docker exec -it api bash`, so it prompted on every test run inside a container. The guard classifies the inner command instead, and still asks when the inner command is an interactive shell.
`git branch -a` is a listing and `git branch -d` is a deletion; the rule saw one verb. The guard tells creation, deletion and moving apart from listing.
same shape: `git worktree list` reads, everything else writes. The guard makes that distinction.
a plain GET is how a change gets checked. The guard detects the write forms — -X/--method with POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, and the -f/-F field flags that make gh POST implicitly.
the same reasoning as gh api.

this denied `git stash list` and `git stash show`, which read shelved work and change nothing. A denial cannot be clicked through, so this blocked ordinary inspection outright. The floor now denies the writing subcommands by name, including bare `git stash`, which means push.
this denied `git remote -v`, one of the most common read-only commands there is. The floor now denies add, remove, rename, set-url, set-head, set-branches, prune and update by name.
